research_question: How much does synchronized IMU motion information improve wrist-PPG heart-rate estimation, particularly under increasing motion corruption?
dataset_source: https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/495/ppg+dalia (original per-subject distribution, NOT the Zenodo .ts mirror, which lacks a subject/group field)
dataset_citation: Reiss, A., Indlekofer, I., Schmidt, P., & Van Laerhoven, K. (2019). Deep PPG: Large-scale Heart Rate Estimation with Convolutional Neural Networks. MDPI Sensors, 19(14), 3079.
ground_truth_source: Real ECG-derived HR from PPG-DaLiA's own data['label'] array (chest RespiBAN device), one value per 8s/2s-step window - not computed by this project

window_parameters.synchronization: PPG and IMU windows share the same absolute start time t0 = window_index * step_seconds from recording start; each stream is sliced at its own native sample rate from that same t0 (no resampling to a common rate, no interpolation); the real HR label at the same window_index is used as ground truth for that window, per the original dataset creators' own windowing convention (verified: (recording_duration_s - 8) / 2 + 1 == len(label) exactly on real subject S1)

preprocessing.ppg: per-window z-score (window mean subtracted, divided by window std); windows with std < 1e-8 (flat/dropped sensor segment) are dropped, not fabricated
preprocessing.imu: per-axis, per-window z-score (each of x/y/z independently mean-zeroed and unit-variance within its own window)

hr_target_normalization.method: z-score using TRAINING-SET-ONLY mean/std (never derived from validation or test subjects)
hr_target_normalization.note: Model output is normalized; real bpm = model_output * std + mean

preprocessing.motion_energy_feature: std of raw (non-normalized) accelerometer magnitude within the window - used only for stratified reporting, not as a model input

model_b_ppg_plus_imu.description: Conv1DEncoder(ppg, in_channels=1) + Conv1DEncoder(imu, in_channels=3) -> ModalityFusionTransformer(n_modalities=2, n_heads=4, n_layers=1) -> Linear(embedding_dim, 1) head

model_c_ppg_plus_shuffled_imu_negative_c.description: Identical architecture to Model B; each subject's own ACC windows randomly permuted among themselves (seed 42), breaking true PPG<->IMU temporal correspondence while preserving per-subject motion statistics

negative_control_metrics.note: Model C uses the same architecture as Model B but with each subject's own ACC windows randomly permuted among themselves, breaking true PPG<->IMU temporal correspondence while preserving per-subject motion statistics. If Model C's MAE is close to Model B's, Model B's gain over Model A may come from IMU carrying generic extra dimensions/population regularities rather than genuine synchronization. If Model C's MAE falls back toward Model A's, that supports synchronization itself mattering. Reported as observed, not adjusted toward either interpretation.

reproducibility.method: Loaded each saved checkpoint state_dict into a fresh model instance and re-evaluated on the held-out test set; compared against the values recorded during training.

limitations: Trained and evaluated on PPG-DaLiA (terrestrial, free-living daily activities), not astronaut or spaceflight data - no microgravity validation.

Held-out test set is 3 subjects (out of 15 total) in this specific seeded split - a different split could shift exact numbers, though the direction of the effect (IMU helps) was consistent across all 3 test subjects individually.

IMU benefit did NOT monotonically increase with motion-quartile severity in this run (largest absolute gain was in the lowest-motion quartile) - reported as observed, not smoothed into a monotonic story.
Per-activity breakdown shows one activity (table_soccer) where Model B performed WORSE than Model A - a real negative result within an overall-positive experiment.
CURRENT MODEL DOES NOT PROVIDE VALIDATED PREDICTIVE UNCERTAINTY. Model output is a single point estimate; no variance/confidence head exists or has been calibrated.
This experiment establishes heart-rate estimation performance only - it does not establish anything about stress, fatigue, cognitive load, or other targets.

ModalityFusionTransformer was generalized during this experiment to accept an explicit n_modalities parameter (previously hard-coupled to the dashboard's global 4-modality tuple) - default behavior for existing dashboard callers is unchanged and covered by backend/tests/test_models.py.
